annotations.text:
Round 1: six aesthetic directions for the firmware Home screen. Outcome: B (Ink Bar) chosen as the base, refined on the B Variants page; the V1 theme is B2 · Quiet.
All artboards are exact panel size (480x800, Xteink X4 portrait), strict black/white; dot patterns stand in for dithered grays.

A · Quiet Classic — bookish serif (Literata), hairline rules, hard offset shadows. Chrome recedes; typography carries the brand.
Tradeoff: understated — risks feeling anonymous.

B · Ink Bar — geometric sans (Space Grotesk), heavy black bars, big numerals, blocky buttons. Confident, device-like, very legible focus states.
Tradeoff: loud chrome competes with book covers.

C · Editorial — serif + mono pairing, masthead rules, dotted leaders like a table of contents. Literary and distinctive.
Tradeoff: densest of the three; mono metadata may feel fussy at e-ink sizes.

All eight V1 screens in the chosen theme: B2 · Quiet (Space Grotesk chrome, hairline rows, black fill = focus). Book body text stays Literata — content typography belongs to reader settings, not the theme. Inverted rows show button-navigation focus; there is no touch. Book content is Middlemarch (public domain). Instapaper/Articles is V2 — see the V2 page.

D · Terminal — command-line reader: Space Mono, inverse-video focus, segmented progress cells, dotted leaders. Unapologetically hacker.
Tradeoff: mono eats width; long titles truncate fast.

E · Playbill — Victorian handbill: IM Fell English, double-rule frame, stacked centered type, diamond ornaments, period copy. The device as a printed object.
Tradeoff: centered layout fights long metadata; the voice is a commitment.

F · Spine — constructivist poster: rotated book-spine title (Archivo Black), giant percent numeral, hard diagonal, condensed menu. Boldest hierarchy of the six.
Tradeoff: rotated text costs a beat of readability; loudest chrome.

Direction B (Ink Bar) won as the default-theme base, and B2 · Quiet was picked as the V1 theme — the V1 Screens page is styled with it. Themes can also change layout structure entirely, so louder ideas (like F) can ship as selectable themes post-V1.
B · Base — the original Ink Bar, unchanged, for side-by-side comparison.

B1 · Spine — F's signature move in B's register: black spine band with the title set vertically in Space Grotesk; big percent numeral instead of a cover.
Tradeoff: no cover art on Home.

B2 · Quiet — B's geometry with lighter chrome: white header with a rule instead of a black bar, hairline menu rows, dot-dither cover. Easier to live with daily.
Tradeoff: less of B's punch; focus relies on the single filled block.

B3 · Inverted — the whole theme flipped white-on-black (the display driver supports polarity inversion, so this is nearly free to ship as a theme).
Tradeoff: full black fields cost refresh ghosting and look patchy on some e-ink panels.

Every remaining UX path in the B2 theme: empty and error states, hold-action menus, reader tools, and the on-demand Wi-Fi flow.
Hint bars always show 4 slots, one per hardware button (Back / Confirm / Up / Down); a button with no action leaves its slot empty, and a hold action stacks inside its button's slot.
Row 4: the full Wi-Fi joining path — scan, password entry, failure, hotspot setup, and sync feedback.
Row 5: end-of-book, battery-empty, and boot states (the Instapaper boards moved to the V2 page).
Empty & missing: first-run Home points at the two loading paths. If the current book disappears (SD card edited elsewhere), Home falls back to the most recent existing book and says why once.

Hold Confirm on a list item opens contextual actions (library: open / details / mark finished / delete; articles: read / archive / like). Destructive actions always get a confirm step and never erase reading progress.
Wi-Fi is strictly on-demand: Wi-Fi is off except during book transfers and setup. The connect dialog appears when an action needs the network, and Wi-Fi turns off when it finishes.

Joining a network on-device: scan list, then a button-driven keyboard (Up/Down between rows, side page buttons along a row, Confirm types, Back deletes / hold cancels). The setup hotspot is the no-typing alternative and also carries Instapaper sign-in via the web page. Failure states say Wi-Fi is off again.

The browser side of the product, served by the device itself: drag-and-drop book uploads and the Setup page (Wi-Fi networks). Same voice as the firmware. Typing happens here, so nothing needs typing on the device.

Instapaper was cut from V1 on 2026-08-20 to keep the first release achievable — these boards are finished design waiting for V2, not V1 scope.
The flow: Articles opens "not set up" -> the device shows a QR/URL -> the user signs in on the device-served web page (nothing typed on the device) -> the device keeps only an access token and syncs. Reading is offline; archive/like queue locally and push on the next sync.

Peek — book text over the veiled page you are on, so a jump never costs you your place. It is what makes Contents and Bookmarks (this row) worth having: a jump that loses your position is one readers learn not to make.
Inset, so the column is narrower, so the text re-wraps — which is why it says CH. 01 · 4% and not a page number. GO HERE still lands exactly: the cursor travels and the page number is counted on arrival.
Eight lines by design. Content-sized at eleven it filled the glass and stopped reading as a modal.

Reader · Anchored — the Reader with somewhere to go back to. The footer's middle slot holds the return anchor and the progress bar yields it: at 21px the bar plus both counters overrun the 444px of usable width, and the bar is only a graphical restatement of the percentage beside it.
Set by paging BACKWARD as much as by a jump — that is the common way to lose a place. The mark is the kUp icon, not a glyph: U+2191 is outside fontc.py's subset and would render as a notdef box.
Reader.dc.html stays the no-anchor state, unchanged: that is the common case.

Names — "who's this character again?", answered on a device with no network and no pointer. The list is built by scanning each chapter as its pages are counted, so it knows only what you have read: spoiler-proof by construction, and the band's right slot states that boundary rather than a count.
It says NAMES, not CHARACTERS. A capitalisation heuristic cannot tell a person from a place, so LOWICK and MIDDLEMARCH are correct entries.
Alphabetical, which inverts the obvious order: the name you cannot place is rare, so most-mentioned-first buries exactly what you came for.
Confirm opens a PEEK at the introducing sentence — there is no detail screen.

Names · Empty — a variant, not a second screen: same ScreenId, same view model, same band, copy where the rows would be. A book opened at chapter one legitimately knows almost nothing, and the copy names the mechanism (reading fills it) rather than just reporting emptiness — otherwise a reader concludes the feature is broken.
No action slab: nothing here can be pressed to help, and a primary action that cannot work is worse than none.
